## Tutorials

The Date() function returns the current system date.

None.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT CustomerName, Date() AS CurrentDate
FROM Customers;

---

Date()
```

## Tutorials

The DateAdd() function adds a time/date interval to a date and then returns 
the date.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT DateAdd("yyyy", 2, #22/11/2017#);

---

DateAdd(
interval
,
number
,
date
)

---

SELECT DateAdd("yyyy", 1, Date());

---

SELECT LastName, DateAdd("m", 6, BirthDate) FROM Employees;
```

## Tutorials

The DateDiff() function returns the difference between two dates.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT DateDiff("yyyy", #13/01/1998#, #09/05/2017#);

---

DateDiff(
datepart
,
date1
,
date2
,
firstdayofweek
,
firstweekofyear
)

---

SELECT DateDiff("m", #13/01/1998#, #09/05/2017#);

---

SELECT DateDiff("d", #13/01/1998#, Date());
```

## Tutorials

The DatePart() function returns a specified part of a date, as an integer.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT DatePart("yyyy", #09/05/2017#);

---

DatePart(
datepart
,
date
,
firstdayofweek
,
firstweekofyear
)

---

SELECT DatePart("m", #09/05/2017#);

---

SELECT DatePart("w", Date());
```

## Tutorials

The DateSerial() function returns a date from the specified parts (year, month, and day values).

### Code Examples

```
SELECT DateSerial(2017, 4, 20);

---

DateSerial(
year
,
month
,
day
)

---

SELECT DateSerial(2017-10, 4-1, 20-5);
```
